articles.author: Tushar
articles.description:
🍳 HostelChef


Turn whatever's in your room into something you can eat.
I built HostelChef for a friend who often has a random collection of ingredients in their hostel room but struggles to figure out what they can actually make with them.
Instead of searching through recipes and trying to find one that matches what they have, HostelChef lets them enter:
Available ingredients
Cooking time
Equipment
Dietary preference
It then generates a simple, practical recipe tailored to their situation.
The goal was simple: make deciding what to cook in a hostel a little less painful.
Live Demo: https://hostelchef.onrender.com
GitHub: tushar-313/HostelChef
HostelChef is built around Gemma 4, Google's open-weight AI model.
The application uses:
React + Vite → FastAPI → Gemma 4

The frontend collects the user's ingredients and constraints, while the FastAPI backend sends them to Gemma with a structured prompt.
Gemma generates a recipe containing:
Recipe name
Description
Required ingredients
Cooking time
Difficulty
Step-by-step instructions
A practical hostel cooking tip
I kept the project intentionally small. The focus wasn't on building another huge recipe platform, but on using an open model to solve one very specific everyday problem.
For a small personal tool like HostelChef, open models make experimentation much more accessible.
Instead of building the application around a proprietary AI service and treating the model as a black box, using an open-weight Gemma model gives developers more flexibility to experiment with the underlying model and build applications around it. It also makes projects like this easier to adapt for different environments, constraints, and use cases.
For me, that's the interesting part of open innovation: a developer can take an openly available model and turn it into something useful for a very specific problem.
Best Use of Gemma
articles.title: My Friend Asked “What Should I Cook?” So I Built HostelChef

Linkerd in Production: 18 Months, 220 Services, Zero Mesh-Wide Outages


We replaced Istio with Linkerd in May 2025. Eighteen months later: zero mesh-wide outages, mTLS on every pod, retries that actually work. Here's the honest comparison.
We ran Istio from 2023 to 2025. Three things broke:
Sidecar memory leak — every Istio sidecar leaked ~5MB/hour. Across 600 pods, that's 3GB/day of garbage.
Control plane instability — istiod crashed every 2-3 weeks, took 5-10 minutes to recover.
Config complexity — VirtualService, DestinationRule, Gateway, ServiceEntry... 14 CRDs, all subtly different.
The straw that broke it: a 4-hour outage where istiod was in a crash loop after a config push. We migrated to Linkerd in 3 weeks.
Rust proxy (linkerd2-proxy). 12MB memory baseline, doesn't leak. We measur…
